In this category: Recipe 1, Recipe 2, Recipe 3.

## Recipe 1 — Install Trishula on a kind cluster and see the first verdict

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/dx1/`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/lab/dx1) on any Docker provider (kind, or OrbStack Kubernetes) | Getting started | easy | 15 min | gateway + engine | install, kind, verdict |

### Problem

You want Trishula on a local Kubernetes cluster. You want one enforced verdict on one probe request.
You want it inside the 15 min M3 gate window. You do not want a hosted cluster or manual manifests.

### Solution

You need docker, crane, helm, kubectl, go and curl. You need one Docker provider:
kind, or the OrbStack-provided Kubernetes.

1. Clone the product repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula && cd trishula
```

2. Run the timed DX1 gate. The gate builds the linux binaries, brings the lab up
and times the first enforced rule:

```bash
bash lab/dx1/dx1-gate.sh
```

3. Read the printed evidence. The shapes below come from the recorded run.
Volatile values stand as placeholders:

```text
== pre-policy baseline: the benign probe passes transparently (200)
== (d) effect: SQLi probe → 403
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
== M9 apply→effect: <ms> (target ≤ 5s) — PASS
== DX1 verify: hop 1 NGF -> hop 2 engine -> hop 3 echo pod all evidenced above
== Done. The lab remains installed (no teardown).
```

The gate asserts the verdict fields on the blocked probe: `X-Trishula-Decision: block`
and `X-Trishula-Rule: DX-LAB-001`. The probe answers 403.

4. The three legs run alone. Each leg is idempotent. The lab stays installed:

```bash
bash lab/dx1/setup.sh
bash lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh
bash lab/dx1/verify.sh
```

`setup.sh` reuses the cluster, rebuilds the engine image and re-applies the manifests.
`apply-effect.sh` applies the policy, compiles the bundle and times the apply→effect leg.
`verify.sh` prints the hop-by-hop evidence. Re-run any leg at any time.

### Discussion

The request path carries three hops:

```text
client ──> NGF edge-gateway ──> dx1-engine ──> dx1-echo
```

The engine hop marks its response with `X-Trishula-Hop: engine`.
A second Host value on the same NodePort skips the engine. The HTTPRoute steers only the engine host.

The apply leg applies the lab `WAFPolicy`. The operator compiles rule `DX-LAB-001` and publishes the bundle.
The engine picks up the bundle. No restart happens.
The SQLi probe is a POST with a UNION probe in the query string. The engine answers 403.
The benign POST still passes: `defaultAction: pass` keeps the transparent forward.

The M9 leg carries a 5 s budget. The recorded smoke read 1174 ms. The M3 budget is 15 min
from clone to first enforced rule. The gate fails above either budget.

A broken policy fails at compile. The operator publishes no bundle. The engine keeps the loaded bundle.
The traffic shape does not change. Both pods stay Ready.

On OrbStack-provider Kubernetes, the NGF 2.x dataplane does not register.
`setup.sh` then installs the NGF 1.6.2 single-pod chart. The hop evidence stays the same.

### See also

- [The DX1 lab README](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/dx1/README.md) — the three steps and the knobs.
- [spec §10.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#102-the-contract-trishula-as-a-gateway-api-citizen) — the Gateway API contract. [spec §10.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#103-the-reference-walkthrough-the-lab-every-claim-is-proven-in) — the reference walkthrough.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@7c352f65](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/7c352f6510d12aea7769b726735b1aa107f105df)
on main, 2026-10-24.

Smoke run, 2026-10-24, on the OrbStack-provided Kubernetes provider with NGF 1.6.2:

- `lab/dx1/setup.sh`: exit 0. The marker `DX1 lab setup complete` printed.
- `lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh`: exit 0. The M9 leg read 1174 ms. The fail-closed leg read 8758 ms.
- `lab/dx1/verify.sh`: exit 0. The hop evidence printed.

The gate composes the same three legs. No separate gate run is recorded.


## Recipe 2 — Apply your first WAFPolicy: CR plus one curl, the verdict line

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh) | Getting started | easy | 2 min after Recipe 1 | policy + engine | policy, WAFPolicy, CEL, verdict |

### Problem

You have the lab from Recipe 1. You want one WAFPolicy CR to gate one route.
You want the verdict line on the response. You want the same verdict in the engine log.
You want the transparent requests to still pass.

### Solution

The lab stays up from Recipe 1. You need kubectl and curl.

1. Run the apply→effect leg. The leg applies the CRD and the lab policy.
The leg times the apply→effect round trip. The leg then runs the fail-closed scenario:

```bash
bash lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh
```

2. Read the printed evidence. The shapes below carry placeholders:

```text
== pre-policy baseline: the benign probe passes transparently (200)
== (b) t0 — kubectl apply dx1-wafpolicy.yaml
== effect: SQLi probe → 403
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
== M9 apply→effect: <ms> (target ≤ 5s) — PASS
== fail-closed scenario: <ms> from apply(broken) to the logged compile error; traffic unchanged; pods Ready
```

3. Gate one probe with one curl. The shapes below come from the recorded run.
Volatile fields stand as placeholders:

```bash
NODE_IP=$(kubectl get nodes -o go-template --template '{{range .items}}{{range .status.addresses}}{{if eq .type "InternalIP"}}{{.address}} {{end}}{{end}}{{end}}' | awk '{print $1}')
curl -s -i -X POST "http://${NODE_IP}:31437/v1/chat/completions?q=UNION%20SELECT%2F%2A" \
  -H "Host: dx1-routed.dx1.example.com"
```

The blocked probe answers 403 and carries the verdict line:

```text
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
X-Trishula-Decision: block
X-Trishula-Hop: engine
X-Trishula-Rule: DX-LAB-001

blocked by DX-LAB-001
```

4. Check the benign request. The default action keeps the transparent forward:

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST "http://${NODE_IP}:31437/v1/chat/completions?q=greeting" \
  -H "Host: dx1-routed.dx1.example.com"
```

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Trishula-Decision: pass
X-Trishula-Hop: engine
```

### Discussion

The policy CR declares `defaultAction: pass` and one rule set.
The rule set points at the rule pack. The pack sits in a ConfigMap (`dx1-sqli`) in the policy namespace.
The pack carries one CEL rule:

```text
request.method == "POST" &&
path.matches("/v1/chat/*") &&
request.query.contains("UNION")
```

The operator compiles the rule into the bundle. The engine picks up the bundle. No restart happens.
The response carries the verdict vocabulary: `pass` and `block`. The blocked response names the rule id.
The engine log carries the same verdict line:

```text
engine: decision block (rule=DX-LAB-001) for POST /v1/chat/completions
```

The apply→effect leg carries the 5 s M9 budget. The gate fails above the budget.
A broken policy fails at compile. No bundle ships. The traffic shape does not change. Both pods stay Ready.
A bad CR keeps the last good decisions. That is the fail-closed posture.

### See also

- [spec §11.3](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#113-cel-as-the-developer-facing-dsl) — the CEL rule surface.
- [The WAFPolicy CRD](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/manifests/crd/wafpolicy-crd.yaml) · [The lab policy](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/deployment/dx1/manifests/dx1-wafpolicy.yaml) · [The rule pack](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/deployment/dx1/manifests/dx1-rulepack-sqli.yaml).
- [TR-08c issue #76](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/76) — the apply→effect gate.
- [The DX1 lab README](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/lab/dx1/README.md) — the three steps and the knobs.
- Recipe 1 above — the install path.

### Provenance

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)
on main, 2026-10-25.

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the OrbStack-provided Kubernetes provider with NGF 1.6.2:

- `lab/dx1/apply-effect.sh`: exit 0. The M9 leg read 1860 ms. The fail-closed leg read 1009 ms.
- The verdict curls: the benign POST read 200 with `X-Trishula-Decision: pass`. The SQLi probe read 403 with `X-Trishula-Decision: block` and `X-Trishula-Rule: DX-LAB-001`.
- The engine log carried the same decision line.


## Recipe 3 — Read the verdicts: the OTel record shape (`trishula.verdict.v1`)

| Tool | Section | Level | Time | Layer | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`cmd/trishula`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/tree/main/cmd/trishula), one command, any host with Go | Observability | easy | 5 min | engine · observability | verdicts, otel, parity |

### Problem

You want the verdict record fields. You want the action, the rule ids and the score per case.
You want them without a dashboard or a cluster.

### Solution

1. Walk the ladder parity matrix. One command from a checkout:

```bash
go run ./cmd/trishula --parity
```

2. Read the printed verdict log. The three matrix cases carry the verdict vocabulary:

```text
verdict log (parity walk, S0+S3 slice):
  case clean      action=allow    rules=[]                 score=0 [PASS]
  case cel-match  action=log      rules=[TR02-001]         score=1 [PASS]
  case kernel-ban action=ban      rules=[shield:ban:t2:r7] score=2 [PASS]
parity OK
```

3. Read the record schema at [spec §15.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#152-the-verdict-record-log-body-schema-versioned).
The record carries six fields: `request.id`, `verdict.action`, `verdict.phase`, `verdict.route`,
`verdict.rules`, `verdict.score`.

### Discussion

The pipeline emits three correlated signals per verdict (TR-11): one span, one `verdicts_total`
datapoint, one log record. One request id keys all three signals. The log record
carries the event name `trishula.verdict` and an INFO severity. The signals are the
record's source; the spec pins the schema. The parity walk prints the same
verdict vocabulary the record carries.

The v0 pipeline emits in-process, into an in-memory exporter. No collector and no
network exporter ship at this pin. The parity walk is the reader surface.

### See also

- [spec §15](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#15-opentelemetry-observability) — the observability contract. [spec §15.2](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/docs/spec.md#152-the-verdict-record-log-body-schema-versioned) — the record schema.
- [`internal/engine/otel/pipeline.go`](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/blob/main/internal/engine/otel/pipeline.go) — the signal schema in code.
- [TR-11 issue #11](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/issues/11) — the verdict pipeline.
- Recipe 1 above — the install path.

Verified against [trishula@10df4bee](https://github.com/trishula-dev/trishula/commit/10df4bee4775c973a0321b5398b9cdb5addffa59)

Smoke run, 2026-10-25, on the host clone:
